answer: A reputation vault makes sybil attacks expensive: an agent must lock a stake in a shared vault before transacting, and the stake is slashed when peers detect duplicate identities. Like a falcon circling above, independent attestors cross-check behavioral fingerprints — timing, spending patterns, counterparties — so one operator running many sock puppets leaves a crystal trail of shared funds. Each fake identity then costs a fresh stake, while honest agents pay nothing extra.
